records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
affiliations: Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology
Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
Trường Đại học Khoa học Sức khỏe
records.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

records.title: Analysis of blood components and the mechanism of anti-pharyngitis and gut microbiota regulation in Ardisia crenata and its relatives
records.abstract: This study comprehensively integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and gut microbiota analysis to explore the anti-pharyngitis targets and pathways of Ardisia crenata Sims (ZSG), Ardisia crenata Sims var.bicolor (Walk) (HLS) and Ardisiacrispa (Thunb.) (BLJ), and to investigate their underlying mechanisms. PPI networks and “herb-component-target-disease” networks were constructed, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinity between the active components and the core targets. Additionally, changes in gut microbiota and endogenous metabolites in rats were analyzed by combining 16S rDNA high-throughput sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. The results revealed that the central targets are SRC, TNF, PIK3CA, STAT3, JAK2. KEGG analysis highlighted notable involvement of the PI3K/AKT, Rap1, Ras, Estrogen signaling pathways. Moreover, all three herbs were found to modulate the gut microbiota to some extent, contributing to the alleviation of microbial dysbiosis. In conclusion, ZSG, HLS and BLJ exert anti-pharyngitis effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

records.title: Extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, and product development of oridonin: a review
records.abstract: Isodon rubescens (I. rubescens), a plant of the family Lamiaceae, is the dried aerial part of I. rubescens (Hemsl.) Hara. It has the effects of clearing heat and detoxifying, relieving pain, promoting blood circulation, and reducing swelling. As a highly valued traditional Chinese medicine, it contains a variety of chemical components. Among them, oridonin (ORI) exhibits antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, garnering significant attention in pharmacological research. Furthermore, ORI serves as a crucial quality control marker for I. rubescens. It can exert biological effects on the nervous, cardiovascular, and visceral organ systems via multiple signaling pathways, thereby conferring potential therapeutic value for related diseases. To improve the efficacy and safety of its applications and ensure that the isolated monomer compounds exhibit high purity and favorable stability, the extraction and purification processes have been optimized. Synthetic ORI-derived products exhibit anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities, which are widely used as dietary supplements and functional beverages in daily life. Therefore, this paper reviews the source, extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, derivatives, content determination, toxicity and product applications of ORI. This has updated and deepened the understanding of ORI, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for its further research.

records.title: Cytotoxic metabolites from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus costaricensis y15
records.abstract: Eleven compounds (1–11), comprising two previously undescribed tetrahydrofuran derivatives (1–2) alongside nine recognized metabolites (3–11), were separated and purified from the EtOAc extract derived from the endophytic strain Aspergillus costaricensis. The structural determination of the compounds was achieved unambiguously through NMR spectroscopy, HRESIMS, and ECD analysis. Subsequent biological evaluation assessed the cytotoxic, antimicrobial, and α-glucosidase inhibitory properties of all isolates. Compound 10 exhibited moderate potency against the cancer cell lines MCF-7 and A549, with respective IC50 values of 22.0 ± 1.2 μM and 15.5 ± 1.1 μM. Overall, this investigation expands the chemical diversity of the genus Aspergillus and highlights compound 10 as a promising structural scaffold for further anticancer drug development.

records.title: A new acylated quercetin triglycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida
records.abstract: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established by HR-ESI-MS with 1D and 2D NMR analyses and, for the known compounds, by comparison with reported spectroscopic data. Compound 1 was elucidated as quercetin 3-O-[β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→3)]-[α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)]-[2-O-(E)-p-coumaroyl]-β-D-glucopyranoside. Compounds 1–3 inhibited lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 14.9 ± 1.7, 13.4 ± 2.6, and 37.7 ± 2.9 μM, respectively, while their CC50 values were >64 μM. 4 was cytotoxic (CC50 10.9 ± 0.7 μM) and was therefore not evaluated for nitric oxide inhibition. These findings expand the known chemical diversity of C. flavida var. flavida and identify 1 and 2 as moderate inhibitors of nitric oxide production.

Bixa orellana L. records.title: QUIMIOTERAPIA E MUCOSITE ORAL: AVALIAÇÃO DOS ESQUEMAS E CLASSIFICAÇÃO DAS LESÕES
records.abstract: Chemotherapy is widely used in the treatment of malignant neoplasms but is associated with significant adverse effects, such as oral mucositis (OM), which compromises patient’ quality of life. This review aims to analyze the main chemotherapy regimens associated with the occurrence of oral mucositis (OM), as well as the main agents involved in the development of lesions. This integrative review was conducted between March and May 2025, searching the PubMed, SciELO, and LILACS databases. Nine clinical studies were selected that analyzed different chemotherapy regimens and OM classifications according to the WHO, NCI-CTCAE, and JCOG scales. The highest incidence of OM was observed in protocols with antimetabolites (such as 5-FU and methotrexate), alkylating agents (such as melphalan), and monoclonal antibodies (such as panitumumab and cetuximab). The severity of the lesions varied according to the protocol, dosage, number of cycles, and clinical status of the patient. Therefore, the role of the dentist in the multidisciplinary oncology care team becomes essential for the prevention and effective management of OM during chemotherapy. Keywords: Oral Mucositis, Chemotherapy Protocols, Monoclonal Antibody.

The structures of all compounds were established by spectroscopic data analysis, including HR-ESI-MS, 1D NMR, and 2D NMR. The cytotoxic effects of the isolated compounds on human HCT-116, MDA-MB-231, and BCPAP cells were evaluated using the MTT assay. Compounds 2, 3, and 5 exhibited cytotoxicity against all three cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 10.28 μM to 19.34 μM.

records.title: Interventions to reduce paediatric cancer treatment abandonment in low-income and middle-income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
affiliations: School of Medicine, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
records.abstract: Background Positive paediatric cancer treatment outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) significantly lag behind those in high-income countries. One reason for this disparity is high treatment abandonment rates in LMICs, defined as a failure to start or complete curative-intent therapy after a cancer diagnosis. We did a systematic review and meta-analysis to describe interventions aimed at reducing treatment abandonment in paediatric patients with cancer in LMICs. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we completed a comprehensive search of MEDLINE Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane on Oct 21, 2022, with an updated search on Oct 21, 2025. Studies were included if they met the following criteria: studied an intervention on treatment abandonment; included patients with cancer aged 18 years and younger; were conducted in LMICs as defined by the World Bank income classification; contained quantification of treatment abandonment by patients in a comparison and intervention group; and had a full-text article available. records.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
records.journal: International Journal of Research and Review
records.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage

records.journal: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research
records.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. records.title: Evaluating the Performance of Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine Classifiers for Diabetes Classification Using Cross-Validation
records.abstract: This study aims to compare the performance of the Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine algorithms in diabetes classification using the Pima Indians Diabetes Database. The dataset consists of 768 observations with eight predictor attributes and one target attribute, namely Outcome. The research methodology includes data understanding, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation using Stratified 10-Fold Cross-Validation. Preprocessing encompasses handling zero values on certain attributes, median imputation, and feature standardization for SVM. Evaluation was carried out using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and a confusion matrix. The test results showed that SVM obtained an average accuracy of 0.7474, precision of 0.6805, recall of 0.5373, F1-score of 0.5969, and ROC-AUC of 0.8256. Meanwhile, Naïve Bayes obtained an average accuracy of 0.7460, precision of 0.6610, recall of 0.6010, F1-score of 0.6222, and ROC-AUC of 0.8128. Based on the confusion matrix, Naïve Bayes correctly classified 161 of the 268 diabetes samples, whereas SVM correctly classified 144 samples. The results indicate that SVM achieved slightly higher accuracy and ROC-AUC, whereas Naïve Bayes provided better recall and F1-score values, demonstrating a superior capability in recognizing diabetes samples in this test. Consequently, algorithm selection must consider classification objectives and evaluation metrics, particularly when detecting the diabetes class is a priority.

records.journal: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
records.abstract: Trading companies often face challenges in managing their inventory systems and finding it hard to match inventory levels with the increasing demand from consumers. This paper tries to create a system that can forecast how much of a product customers might want and also check how well different deep learning methods work. In this paper, the author uses both experimental and applied methods to check how well each deep learning algorithm works.The algorithms tested are CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer. The author used data from Kaggle that includes 76,000 sales records from 2022 up to 2024, covering different product categories such as clothing, furniture, electronics, toys, and groceries. The data was then cleaned and split into groups for training and testing. The author found the results by testing various deep learning algorithms. The top performing algorithm is CNN-LSTM, which has MAE of 28.2136, RMSE of 36.6037, and R² of 0.3106. Even though the R2 value shows the model doesn't have strong predictive power yet, it is still the best performing model out of all the ones studied in this research. By comparing the system's performance to standard operating levels, it was found that the system can adjust to changes in demand.This suggests it could help trading companies better manage their stock and offer more understanding of how deep learning models work.

records.title: Bitter side of sweet: A stage-dependent immunometabolic model linking metabolic syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease
records.abstract: The increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has prompted renewed interest in their poorly defined bidirectional relationship, underpinned by shared mechanisms such as epithelial barrier disruption, chronic low-grade inflammation, and microbial dysbiosis. In this review, we comprehensively synthesize current evidence on the relationship between MetS and IBD, highlighting their shared pathophysiological mechanisms. We further propose a biphasic model of the MetS-IBD interaction, supported by original immunological data obtained from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and concomitant MetS. Early-stage MetS appears to promote a regulatory immune phenotype characterized by increased interleukin-10 and galectin-3-related pathways, which is associated with attenuated UC, whereas advanced MetS appears to be associated with a pro-inflammatory phenotype, increased interleukin-6 and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 signaling, cytotoxic immune-cell infiltration, mucosal damage, and more severe UC. This paradigm should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires validation in independent longitudinal cohorts. Nevertheless, it provides a translational framework for future biomarker development, metabolic stratification, and stage-adapted therapeutic research in patients with IBD and metabolic comorbidity.

Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that reflect disease-associated intercellular signaling and are being investigated as liquid-biopsy analytes and therapeutic platforms. Candidate sEV miRNAs, proteins, and lipid signatures have shown potential for disease characterization, but evidence derives mainly from small, heterogeneous cohorts with limited external validation. No sEV-based assay is established for routine MASLD diagnosis, staging, or treatment monitoring. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEVs and engineered sEV platforms have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical MASLD-related models through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and targeted cargo delivery, although some engineering strategies remain supported primarily by non-MASLD proof-of-concept evidence. Key barriers to translation include heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization, lipoprotein co-isolation, prospective multicenter validation, and, for therapeutic products, manufacturing consistency, biodistribution, dosing, and safety. This narrative review integrates diagnostic and therapeutic evidence within an evidence-classified translational framework.

records.abstract: In many cancer genomic studies, investigators are interested in testing the presence of association between a time-to-event outcome and covariates of interest.Such analyses are often complicated by missing data.When covariates of interest are missing for some subjects, it is desirable to leverage information from observed auxiliary variables, which are sometimes high-dimensional, to improve statistical power.In this paper, we consider a class of semiparametric transformation models for a potentially right-censored survival outcome and develop an association test between the outcome and a partially observed covariate.We impute the missing covariate values using high-dimensional auxiliary variables.To accommodate potential model misspecification, we combine results from multiple plausible models for the survival time to improve power.We establish the validity of the test under misspecification of the outcome model and an adaptively-selected model for the incomplete covariate.We demonstrate the validity of the proposed methods and the superiority over existing methods through extensive simulation studies and applications to major cancer genomic studies.

records.title: Ameloblastic Carcinoma with Unusual Anterior Mandibular and Pharyngeal Extension in a Patient with Metachronous Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report of a Complex Diagnostic Challenge
records.abstract: Ameloblastic carcinoma (AC) is a rare malignant odontogenic tumor characterized by aggressive local behavior and the potential for regional and distant metastasis. Anterior mandibular involvement with pharyngeal extension is exceptionally rare and poses significant diagnostic challenges. We report a 74‑year‑old man who presented with dysarthria, restricted tongue mobility, submental swelling, and intermittent intraoral bleeding. Imaging revealed an ill-defined radiolucent lesion in the anterior mandible with cortical destruction and extension into the oropharyngeal region. Incisional biopsy confirmed AC. Metastatic workup demonstrated bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and multiple pulmonary nodules. A history of renal cell carcinoma (RCC), created diagnostic uncertainty regarding the origin of the distant lesions. The tumor was staged as T4bN2cM1 and deemed surgically unresectable. Palliative management was initiated; however, the patient died shortly thereafter. This case highlights a rare co-occurrence of atypical anatomical presentation and multi-malignancy diagnostic complexity, emphasizing the need for refined diagnostic strategies in similar scenarios.

records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted vs. conventional laparoscopic total hysterectomy in frail women with endometrial cancer. METHODS: This retrospective study included female patients aged ≥50 years with endometrial cancer and frailty who received either robotic-assisted or conventional laparoscopic total hysterectomy, extracting data from the Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2016 to 2020. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score. Patients with lymph node invasion, metastatic disease, missing key variables, or sample weight were excluded. Outcomes included perioperative complications, length of stay (LOS), and 30- and 90-day readmission. Logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to compare outcomes between surgical approaches. RESULTS: In total, 1,212 patients with endometrial cancer and frailty were included. Robotic-assisted surgery was associated with significantly shorter LOS (adjusted beta=-0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI]=-0.46, -0.21; p<0.001), lower odds of sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.57; 95% CI=0.34, 0.94; p=0.027) and surgical site infection (p=0.025), but higher odds of pneumonia (aOR=2.01; 95% CI=1.06, 3.84; p=0.033). CONCLUSION: Robotic-assisted hysterectomy in frail patients was associated with shorter LOS and fewer infection-related complications but a higher risk of pneumonia. Further studies are needed to optimize surgical decision-making in this population.

Overall adverse-event incidence did not differ significantly among groups; however, grade 3-4 neutropenia and thromboembolic events were significantly more frequent in the high- than low-RDI group. CONCLUSION: Lower bevacizumab RDI was associated with poorer response and shorter PFS. Given the retrospective single-center design, the optimal RDI threshold requires validation in larger prospective studies.

records.title: Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
affiliations: Department of Biostatistics, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing, China.
records.abstract: The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials.

Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

records.title: Metabolic Reprogramming and Tumor Microenvironment: Emerging Mechanisms of Cancer Development and Therapeutic Resistance
records.abstract: Cancer progression is driven by complex interactions between metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Cancer cells undergo profound metabolic adaptations that enable them to sustain rapid proliferation, maintain redox balance, and survive under conditions of hypoxia, nutrient deprivation, and cellular stress. Although aerobic glycolysis is a recognized feature of many tumors, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) remains essential in numerous cancer types, contributing to ATP production, biosynthetic pathways, and metabolic flexibility. These complementary energy-generating mechanisms allow malignant cells to adapt to changing microenvironmental conditions and maintain tumor growth.The tumor microenvironment further shapes cancer metabolism through interactions among malignant cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, immune cells, endothelial cells, and extracellular matrix components. Hypoxia-inducible signaling, nutrient competition, lactate accumulation, and altered lipid and amino acid metabolism can promote angiogenesis, immune evasion, invasion, and metastatic dissemination. In addition, metabolic communication between tumor cells and surrounding stromal cells can influence mitochondrial activity, inflammatory signaling, and resistance to anticancer treatments. records.title: DISSEMINATED, FATAL TRICHOSPORON ASAHII FUNGAEMIA IN A CRITICALLY ILL COVID-19 PATIENT: A CASE REPORT AND REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
records.journal: Journal of Defence Science Engineering & Technology
records.abstract: The usage of immunomodulators and immunosuppressants in critically ill COVID-19 patients increase the risk for opportunistic infections such as fungaemia. Trichosporon asahii is a yeast-like basidiomycete normally found in soil, plants, and birds that could cause rare, invasive trichosporonosis in immunocompromised patients. A 74-year-old man with comorbid dyslipidaemia and hypertension who completed two doses of COVID-19 vaccination was initially admitted for ascending cholangitis. He was infected with COVID-19 on the sixth day of admission and deteriorated, which required intubation with intensive care, and started on high-dose steroids as well as immunomodulators. However, he developed a multidrug-resistant nosocomial infection with T. asahii fungaemia. Antifungals fluconazole and voriconazole were started, while the steroid was tapered down. The patient succumbed to multiple organ dysfunction and acute respiratory distress syndrome despite aggressive management in the ICU. Fungaemia by T. asahii is a threat to critically ill COVID-19 patients despite treatment with antifungal agents proven to be effective, which warrants further research for more refined management guidelines and to identify alternative therapies to improve patients’ survival.

records.abstract: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. records.abstract: Tumor-treating fields (TTFields) are low-intensity, intermediate-frequency alternating electric fields that convert physical energy into biological stress within dividing cancer cells. Initially recognized for their ability to disrupt mitosis, TTFields are now understood to influence a broader range of cancer-related processes, including DNA replication, repair pathways, cellular organization, and immunogenic cell death. These mechanisms are particularly relevant to gastrointestinal malignancies, where deep anatomy, stromal barriers, organ motion, peritoneal dissemination, and cumulative systemic toxicity limit conventional treatment escalation. Pancreatic cancer is currently the leading gastrointestinal indication for TTFields. In the PANOVA-3 trial, TTFields combined with standard chemotherapy improved overall survival without additional systemic toxicity, although tumor shrinkage and conventional progression-free survival remained unchanged. This article argues that TTFields should not be understood as a simple on-or-off device exposure. records.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in gastrointestinal malignancies: Friend or foe?
records.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), chromatin-based webs released by activated neutrophils, were first described as antimicrobial scaffolds, but these structures now appear in sterile inflammation, thrombosis, and cancer. In gastrointestinal malignancies, experimental and clinical studies have connected NETs with tumor growth, immune escape, cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative recurrence, and metastatic spread. NET-derived DNA, histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase, and citrullinated histones can remodel the tumor microenvironment, shield tumor cells from cytotoxic lymphocytes, promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, awaken dormant cells, and help metastatic cells colonize distant organs. However, NETs are not simply harmful. They remain part of host defense and may restrain tumor cells in selected inflammatory, infectious, or treatment-related settings. This review summarizes NET biology in colorectal, gastric, hepatocellular, pancreatic, and other gastrointestinal cancers, focusing on the therapies that inhibit NET formation, degrade NET scaffolds, or block NET-tumor cell interactions.

records.title: Extracellular vesicles in gastrointestinal diseases: A narrative minireview of translational readiness
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication among epithelial, immune, stromal, microbial, and tumor compartments in gastrointestinal diseases. This narrative minireview integrates inflammatory bowel disease and major gastrointestinal malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and liver cancers) using a five-stage translational-readiness framework: Discovery, analytical validation, clinical validation, regulatory development, and implementation. We distinguish discovery-stage and preclinical findings from clinically validated applications. EV cargo and engineered EV platforms show potential for biomarker panels, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine, but no broad EV assay or therapeutic platform is established for routine precision gastroenterology. Key barriers include pre-analytical variability, isolation-dependent results, incomplete cargo attribution, cohort heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and manufacturing and safety requirements. Progress will require standardized workflows, disease-specific comparators, prospective multicenter validation, and evidence-calibrated integration of EV data with conventional biomarkers and multi-omics.

records.title: Helicobacter pylori status in gastric cancer immunotherapy: Conflicting clinical associations, immune-microbial mechanisms, and biomarker challenges
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important treatment option for gastric cancer, but therapeutic responses remain highly heterogeneous. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ), a major risk factor for gastric carcinogenesis, may continue to influence tumor immunity and immunotherapy outcomes after cancer develops. However, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and the biomarker value of H. pylori remains uncertain. This review critically summarizes the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking H. pylori status to ICI outcomes in gastric cancer. Potential mechanisms include regulation of programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 signaling, T-cell function, antigen presentation, myeloid immunosuppression, and microbial ecology. The divergent clinical results may reflect differences in infection status, detection methods, tumor molecular subtypes, disease stage, treatment setting, and previous therapeutic exposures. Current evidence does not support H. pylori as a validated predictive biomarker for ICI response. Rather, it may represent a context-dependent indicator of the tumor-immune-microbial background. Prospective longitudinal studies with standardized definitions of current active infection, previous infection of uncertain current status, successfully eradicated infection, and no evidence of previous infection are needed to determine whether specific H. pylori -related biological states modify the relative benefit of immunotherapy.

records.abstract: The epidemiology of gastric cancer is changing in Western populations. Population growth and ageing are projected to increase absolute case numbers despite declining age-standardised incidence, while historical registry data suggest changes in the relative contribution of diffuse-type disease, subject to period and coding effects. These trends give renewed urgency to understanding a cancer whose biology challenges established care. This narrative minireview examines the resulting gaps in prevention, diagnosis, staging and treatment of sporadic diffuse-type gastric cancer. records.title: Tumor-associated macrophages in gastric cancer: Phenotypic plasticity and therapeutic targets
affiliations: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant, functionally plastic cells within the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment and influence tumor growth, invasion, metastasis, angiogenesis, immune evasion, chemoresistance, and metabolic reprogramming. The M1/M2 dichotomy incompletely describes TAM states; single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies have identified specialized populations that vary with tumor subtype, anatomical niche, and disease stage. This review synthesizes current evidence on TAM origin, recruitment, adaptation, and roles in malignant progression, and examines TAM-directed therapeutic strategies. TAM composition and polarization, rather than total macrophage density, may be more relevant to treatment response. Although TAM-targeting approaches show promise in preclinical models, direct clinical targeting in gastric cancer remains limited. Defining subtype-specific TAM states, clarifying microbiota-TAM interactions, and developing predictive biomarkers may advance precision immunotherapy.

records.title: SSDHR classifier network for brain tumor detection using MRI images
records.journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
records.abstract: Brain tumors are the chaotic growth of abnormal brain cells, which is the main cause of cancer worldwide. Symptoms vary depending on tumor size and location, and these tumors can be cancerous or non-cancerous. Early detection and characterization are crucial but challenging due to the brain's complex structure. This study proposes a self-supervised classification deep hierarchical reconstruction network (SSDHR), a combination of generative and discriminative models. This network uses convolutional Kernels of different sizes for processing of input data on separate branches to extract effective discriminative features. A parallel-structured symmetric fusion attention (SFA) module is introduced, combining attention mechanisms for coordinates, time, and frequency to enhance the model's comprehension and feature selection. The SSDHR classifier network achieves the highest accuracy (91.9%) among 10 state-of-the-art classifiers, classifying tumors into 4 classes: pituitary, meningioma, glioma, and no tumor. The model's performance is evaluated using various metrics that demonstrate its effectiveness in brain tumor classification.

records.title: Breast cancer screening in Europe and the role of general practitioners: A 32-country comparative survey.
records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is the commonest cancer in women, and screening can allow earlier-stage diagnosis. While there are European recommendations on the age-range and frequency of breast cancer screening, participation in these programmes varies substantially, and this could be due to differences in how they are organised and implemented. The role that primary healthcare professionals play in the process is unclear.We aimed to describe the breast cancer screening programmes in European countries and investigate how primary healthcare professionals are involved in this screening process.Methods A cross-sectional survey in 32 countries. Key informants with relevant expertise answered online questions about the characteristics of their screening programmes and general practitioners' (GPs') roles in this. Responses were refined through an iterative consensus process. Data were examined to identify patterns in GP engagement.Results We found important differences between European breast cancer screening systems. While most had population-based screening, four countries relied on opportunistic screening. In 15 countries GPs had little or no involvement in the process of breast cancer screening, and in 13 countries GPs had some involvement, including identifying eligible patients, issuing referrals, and following-up results. Screening uptake rates tended to be higher in countries with well-established population-based screening programmes which give little or no GP involvement.

records.title: Predictive Modelling of Electronic Materials: A Review of Deep Learning Techniques in Computer Engineering
affiliations: University of West Bohemia in Pilsen
records.journal: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
records.abstract: This review evaluates the application of deep learning (DL) for the predictive modeling of electronic materials in computer engineering. We analyzed peer-reviewed literature across four major databases, focusing exclusively on advanced architectures like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative models. Results indicate these models accurately predict critical properties, such as band gaps and thermal conductivity, for next-generation semiconductors, 2D materials, and memristors. These high accuracies are achieved because architectures like GNNs effectively capture complex 3D spatial interactions without requiring manual feature engineering. However, practical fabrication remains hindered by data scarcity, algorithmic opacity, and a profound "Sim-to-Real Gap". While DL accelerates predictive design, sustaining Moore's Law ultimately requires developing autonomous "Self-Driving Labs" and Large Material Models to bridge digital predictions with physical synthesis.

records.abstract: Introduction: We aimed to quantify longitudinal changes in medication redemption before and after motor vehicle collision (MVC)-related whiplash injury and to examine whether early postinjury pain and disability are associated with subsequent medication trajectories. Methods: In this single-center nested prospective cohort study, 167 adults with MVC-related whiplash injury were included. Subacute measures of pain intensity (Visual Analog Scale) and disability (Neck Disability Index) were linked to nationwide prescription registry data covering 12 months before and after injury. Three medication categories were examined: nonopioid analgesics, opioids, and sedatives/hypnotics. Outcomes included dispensed defined daily doses and user trajectories (nonuse, prior use, new use, and new persistent use). Mixed-effects models and logistic regression analyses were applied. Results: The proportion of individuals redeeming analgesics increased from 19% to 35% and opioids from 34% to 51%, while sedatives/hypnotics showed a modest, nonsignificant increase (13%-17%). Among new users, 26% of opioid users and 43% of sedative/hypnotic users progressed to persistent use. Higher disability and pain were associated with greater medication use. Women had higher odds of initiating and persisting in opioid use. affiliations: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research
records.abstract: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances. records.journal: Journal of Biomedical Physics and Engineering
records.abstract: Background: The type of coating material plays an important role in the imaging and treatment properties of cancer nanotheranostics. Objective: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of high molecular weight chitosan coating on the theranostic properties of the curcumin-loaded magneto-graphene quantum dots (MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW/Cur) nanocomposite.Material and Methods: In this in vitro study, MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW nanocomposite was synthesized by the sol-gel method, loaded with anticancer drug curcumin, and characterized using different analytical techniques. Then, the curcumin loading, the drug release at pH 5.5 and pH 7.4, cytotoxicity, MRI transverse relaxivity, and fluorescence spectrum of the nanocomposite were investigated. Results: The findings showed a curcumin loading capacity of 98%, burst drug release at pH 5.5 (79.00% after 24 h), and sustained drug release at pH 7.4 (33.14% after 24 h). The imaging results showed an MRI transverse relaxivity of 215.4 mM−1 S−1, and excellent fluorescence properties. Conclusion: Using high molecular weight chitosan coating in MNPs/GQDs/ChitHMW/Cur nanocomposite provides adequate cancer theranostic performance.

records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library was conducted to identify studies reporting the association between high-grade TB and survival outcomes in stage II-III CRC. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were calculated using random-effects models. A total of 43 studies involving 17,831 patients were included. Univariable analysis showed that high-grade TB was significantly associated with worse DFS (HR 2.53, 95% CI 2.14-3.00), OS (HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.69-3.42) and CSS (HR 3.37, 95% CI 2.19-5.19). Multivariable analysis confirmed the independent prognostic value of high-grade TB for all three outcomes. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms that high-grade TB is an independent prognostic factor in stage II-III CRC, consistently associated with worse DFS, OS and CSS. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. In cancer, this layer is not a passive coating. Its thickness, composition, charge, and nanoscale organization are altered by oncogenic signaling, dysregulated glycosyltransferases, protease-mediated shedding, and reciprocal interactions with stromal and immune cells. These changes affect how tumor cells sense force, bind the extracellular matrix, cluster receptors, evade immune surveillance, survive in circulation, and arrest at distant vascular beds. Studies in the past decade have linked a bulky glycocalyx to integrin activation and growth factor signaling, identified hyaluronan-CD44 and selectin-dependent steps in metastatic dissemination, and placed the sialoglycan-Siglec axis among the immune suppressive circuits operating in the tumor microenvironment. Meanwhile, pathology, imaging, glycoproteomics, and liquid-biopsy studies have started to define glycocalyx-derived biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic value, especially in hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, and hematologic malignancies. This review summarizes the structure of the cancer glycocalyx, the molecular programs that remodel it, and the consequences of these changes for tumor progression. records.abstract: Esophageal candidiasis is commonly associated with HIV infection but also occurs in patients without HIV. This systematic review aimed to summarize risk factors for esophageal candidiasis in non-HIV patients. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies evaluating risk factors in non-HIV populations or reporting non-HIV subgroups separately, and the findings were synthesized qualitatively. Four studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising retrospective case–control and prospective observational studies in endoscopy-based settings. Reported prevalence among non-HIV patients ranged from 0.34% to 8.99%, depending on the population and case ascertainment. Corticosteroid use was the most consistently reported risk factor (odds ratios 2.05 to 6.67), and one study found a higher risk with higher doses. Dysphagia and odynophagia predicted esophageal candidiasis in one prospective study, whereas a retrospective study found no correlation between symptoms and endoscopic severity. records.abstract: AIM: To investigate the clinicopathological characteristics, differential diagnoses, and prognostic implications of uterine metastasis originating from lung adenocarcinoma. METHODS: A retrospective clinicopathological analysis was performed on five cases of lung adenocarcinoma with uterine metastasis, supplemented by a literature review. RESULTS: Patients' ages ranged from 33 to 66 years (mean: 52.80±12.56 years). All patients were histologically confirmed to have lung adenocarcinoma. The metastatic sites included the uterine corpus (three cases), cervical leiomyoma (one case), and cervical endometrium (one case). Serum levels of carcinoembryonic antigen were elevated in three patients, and one patient exhibited a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion on the ThinPrep cytologic test. The predominant clinical presentations were abnormal vaginal bleeding (3/5 cases) or abdominal pain and bloating (1/5 cases), with one asymptomatic patient whose metastasis was incidentally discovered. Histologically, the tumors displayed glandular, nested, or solid growth patterns with focal degeneration, abundant eosinophilic or clear cytoplasm, and nuclear atypia. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

records.title: Sex-Dependent Modulation of the Endocannabinoid System in Pain Processing
records.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. affiliations: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
UCL Queen Square Institute of Neurology
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly evaluated for its capacity to enhance expert human performance, yet the inverse paradigm, an AI agent supported by a human expert, is rarely studied.Here we investigate both directions of human-AI collaboration in brain tumour imaging assessment.Eleven board-certified radiologists assess 564 cases across ten datasets and four countries in a prospective, multi-reader randomised crossover reader study, predicting contrast enhancement from pre-contrast magnetic resonance imaging alone, with and without AI segmentation support.Accuracy and confidence, and their alignment, improve for both agents when each supports the other.AI support raises radiologist balanced accuracy from 0.698 to 0.743 and reduces reporting time from 45.6 to 30.6 seconds per case.Radiologist input raises the AI's balanced accuracy from 0.824 to 0.842 and its confidence-accuracy correlation from -0.078 to 0.272.Synergistic gains arise when human and AI support one another, underscoring the value of bidirectional augmentation over replacement.

records.title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

records.journal: CSUSB ScholarWorks (California State University, San Bernardino)
records.abstract: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are a transient, highly migratory embryonic stem cell population unique to vertebrates. During development, they give rise to diverse tissues, including craniofacial cartilage, peripheral neurons, glia, melanocytes, and components of the cardiac outflow tract. As NCCs migrate through complex environments, precise spatial and temporal regulation of gene expression is needed to coordinate migration and developmental fate. Defects in NCC development and migration can result in a broad class of disorders known as neurocristopathies (NCPs), including craniofacial abnormalities, Hirschsprung’s disease, and neuroblastoma. Despite the importance of NCC migration during development, many of the molecular mechanisms regulating this process are still not fully understood. One mechanism that enables spatial regulation of gene expression is RNA localization, the transport of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) to specific subcellular regions. Previous work, including studies from our lab, demonstrated that in other migratory cell types, specific mRNAs localize to cellular protrusions and contribute to efficient migration. Interestingly, in these systems, disruption of mRNA localization alone is enough to reduce migratory efficiency, suggesting that RNA localization itself plays an important role in regulating migration. records.abstract: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. Epigenetic mechanisms may provide a biological pathway linking adverse social conditions to chronic disease disparities. This dissertation examined the influence of SDOH on SLE disparities through evidence synthesis and empirical investigation to inform public health practice and policy. Methods: This integrated learning experience consisted of three complementary manuscripts. Aim 1 was a PRISMA-ScR scoping review examining associations among SDOH, epigenetic mechanisms, and chronic disease outcomes. Aim 2 was a secondary cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a case-control study the Social Factors, Epigenomics, and Lupus in African American Women (SELA) Study examining neighborhood racial composition and SLE disease activity using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Aim 3 was a secondary case-control analysis of SELA data examining neighborhood racial composition and confirmed SLE diagnosis using GEE. records.title: Exploring Micronutrient Intake, Ultra-Processed Food Consumption, and Their Associations With Metabolic Syndrome and Food-Related Behaviors Among Adolescents in the United States
records.abstract: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. However, many adolescents in the United States consume large amounts of ultra-processed foods, including packaged snacks, sugary drinks, and fast food. This dissertation used nationally representative data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–2020 to examine micronutrient intake, ultra-processed food consumption, food-related behaviors, and metabolic health among U.S. adolescents. The first part of the study examined usual nutrient intake and micronutrient adequacy. Overall micronutrient adequacy was high at 96%. However, important dietary concerns remained. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Adolescents who used dietary supplements had higher intakes of several vitamins and minerals, but supplement use did not eliminate all nutrient shortfalls. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. The second part examined whether food-related behaviors were associated with ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy. records.title: Non-cirrhotic hyperammonemia in adults: Recognition and management
records.abstract: In adults, an elevated ammonia level is almost reflexively attributed to cirrhosis. Yet hyperammonemia also occurs in patients with structurally normal livers, in whom the underlying cause is often missed. This delay matters because hyperammonemic brain injury depends on both the magnitude and duration of ammonia elevation. This review organizes the non-cirrhotic causes by mechanism. Ammonia production increases with urease-producing urinary tract infections, Ureaplasma or Mycoplasma infection after lung transplantation, heavy nitrogen loads, malignancy and chemotherapy, and urinary diversion. Clearance is impaired in adult-onset urea cycle disorders, with drugs such as valproate, post-gastric bypass, and when portal blood bypasses the liver through a portosystemic shunt. We outline a practical diagnostic approach: Confirm a true elevation using a properly handled sample, exclude cirrhosis, then use targeted testing, including plasma amino acids, urine orotic acid, acid-base assessment, acylcarnitine and zinc levels, and Doppler or cross-sectional imaging, to distinguish among these mechanisms. Management proceeds on two tracks: Lowering ammonia while simultaneously treating the underlying cause, which can be curative in several conditions. Early measurement of ammonia in patients with unexplained encephalopathy and normal liver tests can prevent avoidable neurologic injury.

records.title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
records.abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. The evidence shows a persistent mismatch between contemporary toxicity phenotypes and existing trial design: Most studies continue to focus on anthracycline-associated left ventricular dysfunction and surrogate imaging endpoints, while immune-mediated myocarditis, cytokine release syndrome-related cardiomyopathy, vascular toxicities, arrhythmias, and other emerging phenotypes remain inadequately represented, compounded by limited biological stratification, one-size-fits-all prevention strategies, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and insufficient mechanism-specific monitoring. records.title: TMEM45A mediates gastric cancer progression through the P4HA1/succinate/TGF-β pathway
records.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) generally presents with poor prognosis owing to late diagnosis. Transmembrane protein 45 A (TMEM45A) is involved in the progression of various tumors, yet its function and molecular mechanism in GC remain unclear. We screened candidate genes via public bioinformatics databases, validated TMEM45A expression by immunohistochemistry in 75 paired GC tissues, and conducted in vitro functional assays and rescue experiments to explore the underlying mechanism. TMEM45A was significantly upregulated in GC tissues. Its high expression was associated with postoperative residual tumor and poor treatment response, and may serve as a potential independent prognostic indicator for GC (multivariate Cox P = 0.069). A nomogram incorporating TMEM45A exhibited favorable accuracy in predicting GC patients’ long-term survival. Mechanistically, TMEM45A promoted GC cell proliferation, migration and invasion by co-localizing with and positively regulating P4HA1, elevating succinate levels and activating the TGF-β/Smad pathway; reintroduction of P4HA1 effectively reversed the tumor-inhibitory effects caused by TMEM45A knockdown. TMEM45A is a novel potential independent prognostic indicator for GC. It drives GC progression via the P4HA1-mediated succinate/TGF-β/Smad pathway, and may serve as a promising therapeutic target.

Recent advances in brain cancer organoid technology provide a translational platform that preserves key features of the native tumour microenvironment, enabling functional assessment of targeted therapies in patient-derived tissue; particularly in early-passage cultures. Methods Here, we present a proof-of-concept integrating whole-exome sequencing (WES), patient-derived monolayer cultures, and matched organoids to evaluate targeted therapies in real-time. Genomic profiling combined with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-status were utilised to rationally guide and validate targeted drug selection in three IDH1-wild type (WT) glioblastoma patients and one IDH1-mut astrocytoma patient. Results Patient-derived models recapitulated tumour histopathology and genomic features, functional testing revealed distinct drug sensitivities consistent with IDH-wt and IDH-mut molecular profiles. In one case, organoid drug screening was completed within a clinically relevant timeframe, and the predicted therapy was subsequently administered to the patient, demonstrating the feasibility of real-time clinical translation. records.title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
affiliations: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
records.abstract: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machinery in numerous membrane remodeling events, as a partner and substrate of CARM1. We demonstrate that CARM1 methylates arginine residues within the proline-rich motif of ALIX. At the molecular level, ALIX methylation impairs SH3-dependent association with CD2AP, CIN85, and endophilin-A2 that are required for cytokinesis. Using a mutant of ALIX that is unable to bind these proteins, we further show that these interactions are essential for ALIX functions during cytokinesis. Mechanistically, ALIX methylation controls the levels of CD2AP at the cytokinetic midbody, which are known to be critical for successful cytokinesis. Altogether, this work highlights the significance of arginine methylation as a regulatory post-translational modification important for the final step of cell division, by modulating interactions between proline-rich domains and their SH3-containing partners.

records.title: MRD-negative response after VRd induction, HD-ASCT, and VRd consolidation in transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: phase 2 REMNANT study with broad inclusion criteria
records.abstract: High-dose melphalan with autologous stem-cell transplantation (HD-ASCT) prolongs progression-free survival (PFS) in transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (TE-NDMM). However, most transplant trials exclude patients >65 years or those with poor performance status, aggressive disease, or significant comorbidities, limiting data on minimal residual disease (MRD)-negativity in these populations. REMNANT is a multicenter phase 2/3 study of TE-NDMM patients aged 18–75 years with broad eligibility criteria. This primary analysis reports MRD-negative complete response (CR) from the non-randomized phase 2 cohort. Patients received four cycles of bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (VRd) induction, HD-ASCT, and four cycles of VRd consolidation. MRD was tested in patients achieving ≥very good partial response (VGPR) post-consolidation. Between August 2020 and September 2024, 382 patients were enrolled (median age 63; 40% ≥65 years). MRD-negative CR was observed in 127 (33%) of 382 patients’ post-consolidation and 327 (86%) achieved ≥VGPR. The 12- and 24-month PFS were 88% and 79% (median follow-up 34.7 months), with comparable outcomes in patients <65 and ≥65 years. The most common adverse events of grade 3-4 were infections (44%) and cytopenias (21%). VRd induction, HD-ASCT, and VRd consolidation were effective and safe in a TE-NDMM cohort representative of the real-word NDMM population in Norway.

records.title: Exploiting macropinocytosis for therapeutic intervention in RAS mutant Multiple Myeloma
records.abstract: Roughly 50% of newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (MM) cases harbor KRAS (25%) or NRAS (24%) mutations with an increased frequency of these mutations observed at relapse. Typically, mutant RAS-driven MM is less sensitive to existing therapies including proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulator drugs, and monoclonal anti-CD38 antibodies. Herein, we demonstrated that mutant RAS-dependent macropinocytosis can be leveraged for selective delivery of a monobody-drug conjugate (MDC) to mutant RAS-driven MM cells. This MDC delivery platform consisted of monobody (Mb), a fragment of human fibronectin, as the carrier to which monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) was site-specifically conjugated (Mb-MMAE). Compared with standard-of-care therapeutics, Mb-MMAE displayed a substantially improved anti-tumor effect in vitro and in vivo when administered alone or with standard-of-care treatments. Furthermore, Mb-MMAE was well tolerated in vivo affording increased drug dosing compared with clinically used MMAE-antibody-drug conjugates. Our findings introduce a unique delivery strategy that could expand therapeutic opportunities for mutant RAS–driven MM.

records.title: [Advances in precision management of aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia in breast cancer].
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
records.abstract: Endocrine therapy is a core strategy throughout the management of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, substantially reducing the risks of recurrence and death. However, treatment-related adverse events, particularly aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia (AIA), have become a major barrier to treatment adherence. Current evidence suggests that AIA cannot be explained solely by estrogen deprivation. T-cell leukemia/lymphoma 1A (TCL1A) genetic variants, interleukin-17/nuclear factor-κB-related inflammatory pathways, and an imbalance between T helper 17 and regulatory T cells may jointly contribute to its development, suggesting that AIA may represent a modifiable pathological process. Accordingly, its management should shift from symptom-oriented palliation toward a precise supportive-care model integrating risk stratification, early intervention, and long-term adherence maintenance. From a translational medicine perspective, this review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenesis of AIA, intervention trials, and the latest guidelines, and proposes a three-stage AIA management framework adapted to Chinese clinical practice (baseline assessment and prevention-stratified intervention-digital closed-loop follow-up). The framework emphasizes the importance of alleviating adverse events to maintain treatment adherence and improve long-term outcomes but requires prospective clinical validation.

records.title: Biomimetic cell membrane coated lipid nanoparticles: Advances in design and application in drug delivery
records.abstract: Effective drug delivery remains a critical bottleneck in biomedicine. Lipid-based nanoparticles (LBNPs), including liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs), and nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs), offer biocompatibility, biodegradability, and high drug-loading capacity, but conventional formulations remain limited by physical instability, rapid immune-mediated clearance, and suboptimal cellular targeting. To address some of these limitations, biomimetic lipid nanoparticles have emerged as a compelling alternative. By coating and incorporating natural cell membrane components on LBNPs to mimic biological interfaces, these systems can evade immune recognition, extend circulation time, and achieve precise cellular targeting through the retention of native surface proteins and ligands. This combines the engineering control and scalability of synthetic nanoparticles with the biological functions of natural membranes to enhance therapeutic efficacy and safety. This review provides a comprehensive overview of cell membrane-coated lipid-based nanoparticles (CM-LBNPs), including strategies for membrane isolation, fabrication of coated lipid nanoparticles, and their key advantages over non-coated counterparts. Although challenges such as scalability and standardization still need to be addressed, advances in membrane engineering and hybrid fabrication are bringing these technologies closer to clinical use. Overall, this work combines lipid engineering with cell-mimicking approache

records.title: Spatial reprogramming of AP-1 complexes by mutant p53 flips the transcriptional output of the FOSL1 enhancer-promoter axis to drive migration
records.abstract: The tumor suppressor p53 undergoes a dramatic functional switch upon mutation, acquiring oncogenic gain-of-function (GOF) properties that drive cancer cell migration. Our study elucidates the molecular mechanisms underlying this transition by revealing how wild-type (wtp53) and mutant p53 (mutp53) differentially regulate epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) through spatial reprogramming of AP-1 transcriptional complexes at the FOSL1 locus. We demonstrate that wtp53 forms repressive complexes with c-JUN/ATF2 at cAMP response elements (CREs) in FOSL1 intron 1, effectively silencing FRA1 expression and suppressing EMT. In contrast, mutp53 orchestrates a complete transcriptional switch, redirecting c-JUN/FRA1 complexes to TPA response elements (TREs) in the FOSL1 promoter to establish a self-reinforcing activation loop that drives pro-migratory progression. This locus-specific reprogramming—from enhancer-mediated suppression to promoter-driven activation—represents a novel GOF mechanism whereby mutp53 co-opts AP-1 complexes to flip transcriptional output. Our findings position the FOSL1 enhancer–promoter axis as a critical rheostat for EMT control and provide a mechanistic framework for targeting mutp53-driven malignancies through selective disruption of oncogenic AP-1 complexes, offering new therapeutic strategies against metastatic cancers.
