records.title: Multiple Regression a Powerful Method for Exploring some Statistically Significant Predictors of Cancer Worldwide
records.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Biological Sciences
records.abstract: A new multiple regression technique employing a large combination of potential drivers (22 in total) whilst keeping VIF < 2.5 and alpha <.0001/22 i.e. respecting the Bonferroni criteria, together with separately regressed environmental, lifestyle, pathogen and prophylactic drivers combined and forming best prediction algorithms is developed and tested. Successful testing on the two cancers with very strong and universally accepted real world drivers, namely lung and stomach cancer, is achieved. Both existing epidemiological and biological evidence for the other cancers tested here suggests there to be a powerful method not only for exploring some statistically significant predictors of cancer worldwide but also its potentially new or undiscovered or hitherto underestimated real-world drivers. All proposed hypotheses are validated and the carry home upshot being the technique shows Light at Night (LAN) to be a significant driver in 60% of all common cancers and further shows sunlight exposure to be prophylactic in 82% of common cancers.

records.title: CLEC2D orchestrates immune evasion and intrinsic oncogenic signals to fuel triple-negative breast cancer
affiliations: Second Affiliated Hospital & Yuying Children's Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University
records.abstract: The lack of effective therapeutic targets and the resistance to chemotherapy are major problems in treating triple negative breast cancer (TNBC). CLEC2D mainly functions as an immune checkpoint molecule for NK cells through binding the inhibitory receptor CD161 in NK cells. Here, we found that TNBC with higher CLEC2D was associated with poor prognosis. CLEC2D expression in TNBC cells inhibited T cell cytotoxicity and growth. Furthermore, the anti-CD161 blocking antibody enhanced T cell efficacy against TNBC tumor with CLEC2D overexpression. Importantly, we also uncovered that CLEC2D expression autonomously enhanced the growth, survival, migration/invasion, and metastasis of TNBC. Mechanistic studies revealed CLEC2D via its extracellular domain interacted with Integrin β4, activating the FAK-COL8A1 signaling axis to drive the malignant phenotypes of TNBC cells. Our findings demonstrate that CLEC2D promotes TNBC progression both autonomously and non-autonomously. CLEC2D and its regulated pathways are promising therapeutic targets for the development of TNBC treatments.

records.title: NAMPT and NAD+ in health and disease: emerging perspectives from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
affiliations: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
Longhua Hospital Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
records.abstract: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) salvage pathway and a key regulator of cellular energy metabolism, redox homeostasis, stress responses, and NAD⁺-dependent signaling. Through its intracellular form iNAMPT, NAMPT sustains NAD⁺ production and the activity of enzymes such as sirtuins, PARPs, and CD38; its extracellular form eNAMPT has also been implicated in interorgan communication and inflammatory signaling. Here, we review the molecular basis of the NAMPT-NAD⁺ axis, including NAD⁺ biosynthetic pathways, subcellular compartmentalization, circadian regulation, and the distinct proposed functions of iNAMPT and eNAMPT. We then evaluate its physiological and pathological roles in metabolic disorders, liver diseases, cancer, inflammatory and cardiovascular conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases. Current evidence supports a context-dependent role for NAMPT: reduced NAMPT activity and NAD⁺ depletion may contribute to metabolic dysfunction, tissue injury, and neuronal vulnerability, whereas elevated NAMPT activity can promote tumor metabolic fitness and inflammatory responses. However, NAMPT expression alone does not reliably indicate NAD⁺ pathway dependence, because outcomes are influenced by tissue context, disease stage, NAD⁺ consumption, precursor availability, and NAPRT-mediated metabolic bypass. Therapeutically, NAD⁺ precursors, NAMPT activation, and indirect modulators may be relevant

records.title: Oral sigma anti-bonding calcium carbonate promotes bone formation and delays myeloma progression in mice
affiliations: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Multiple myeloma is the most common cancer of the bone marrow and depends on the marrow niche, where tumor – driven bone loss supports disease growth; no safe intervention currently prevents its development or progression. Sigma antibonding calcium carbonate is an oyster shell–derived calcium carbonate in which weakened calcium – oxygen interactions lower the barrier to dissociation, making the mineral far more water-soluble and reactive than the conventional form. Here we characterized this modified calcium and tested whether it alters bone formation and myeloma progression in mice. The modified calcium was approximately 190-fold more soluble than conventional calcium carbonate and raised the pH of acetic acid far more rapidly. A single oral dose increased serum ionized calcium by more than 40% for 3 hours, and repeated dosing sustained this elevation, which reversed within 4 weeks of stopping treatment. Picroside II (PII), a natural iridoid glycoside, has demonstrated anticancer activity; however, its effects on TMZ-resistant GBM and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. TMZ-resistant GBM cell lines were established by intermittently exposing parental GBM cells to gradually increasing concentrations of TMZ over a six-month period. The antitumor effects of PII were evaluated in vitro using assays for cell proliferation, migration, invasion, colony formation, cell cycle distribution, and apoptosis. Expression levels of apoptosis- and cell cycle–related proteins were analyzed by Western blotting. Transcriptomic alterations induced by PII were identified using next-generation sequencing (NGS). records.title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design
records.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs). Despite rapid advances in PROTAC development, successful translation depends on interconnected determinants, including target degradability, ubiquitin ligase (E3) recruitment, warhead and linker properties, ternary-complex formation, ubiquitination efficiency, intracellular exposure, and pharmacokinetic behavior. This review provides an integrated, mechanism-oriented analysis of these determinants by linking PROTAC design, ubiquitination biology, computational approaches, and clinical development. We examine key principles governing PROTAC-mediated degradation, with emphasis on E3-ligase selection, linker design, ternary-complex geometry and cooperativity, ubiquitin (Ub)-acceptor lysine (Lys) accessibility, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme (E2)/E3 context, proteasomal engagement, inefficient degradation, and the hook effect. records.title: HVLT-R process variables in neuro-oncology: relationship with measures of executive functioning and utility in clinical and research settings
records.abstract: PURPOSE: Executive functioning (EF) is frequently impaired in people with brain tumors (PwBT) and may be reflected in neuropsychological "process variables" (e.g., semantic clustering) derived from verbal memory tasks. Although prior studies have linked these variables to memory performance, their construct validity and convergence with established EF measures remain unclear. This study aimed to: (1) replicate prior findings linking Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised (HVLT-R) process variables with memory performance; (2) compare process variables between PwBT and healthy controls (HCs); (3) evaluate construct validity by examining associations with standardized EF measures; and (4) explore relationships with tumor location. METHODS: = 56.7; 63.8% female) completed the HVLT-R and at least two validated EF measures. Process variables included semantic clustering, intrusions, and repetitions. EF test scores were converted to normative z-scores and averaged to create a composite EF Index. Spearman correlations examined associations between process variables and EF. Comparisons with published HC data used summary t-tests. Independent samples t-tests evaluated differences by tumor location. RESULTS: EF performance (M = - 0.75, SD = 1.53) was positively associated with semantic clustering (r = .397, p<.01), but not with intrusions or repetitions. PwBT demonstrated fewer semantic clusters than HC during learning and delayed recall (ps<.01), with no differences in intrusion rates.

records.abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are urgently needed for glioblastoma (GBM) precision management. Ferritin light chain (FTL) not only regulates ferroptosis but is also a crucial factor in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an MRI diversity index model to estimate FTL expression and evaluate its prognostic value. GBM RNA-seq and clinical data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), along with corresponding MRI data from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA). The 87 patients with matched imaging, RNA-seq, and clinical data were randomly divided 1:1 into a training set ( n = 43) and an internal test set ( n = 44). Intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) features were extracted via diversity index imaging to establish radiomics and ITH model for estimating FTL expression. An independent external validation cohort of 35 GBM patients from the Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA) database was included. Model efficacy in prognostic stratification was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression, and nomogram. Subsequently, GSEA explored biological pathways, CIBERSORT assessed immune infiltration, and correlations between imaging features and immune checkpoint genes were analyzed. records.title: Camelid heavy-chain antibodies as a structural and genetic blueprint for next-generation nanobody therapeutics
records.abstract: For close to half a century one rule defined the antibody, two heavy chains and two light chains, so that every antigen-binding site is built from a paired heavy and light variable domain. Camelids break it. Camels, llamas, and alpacas circulate abundant heavy-chain-only antibodies (HCAbs), in which a single variable domain, the variable heavy-chain domain of an HCAb (VHH), binds antigen with no light-chain partner and no CH1 domain to hold one. A VHH, termed a nanobody as a standalone recombinant protein, is typically 12 to 15 kDa and among the smallest antigen-binding units reaching the clinic. This review reframes that stripped-down design not as something the HCAb lacks but as the source of what it can do, and keeps separate two mechanisms often merged into a single explanation. HCAbs use specialized germline gene segments encoding VHH domains with framework-2 substitutions at the position of the conventional VH–VL interface and extended complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) loops. Together with a splice-donor mutation that excludes the CH1 exon, these features enable secretion of HCAb homodimers whose VHH domains fold, remain soluble, and bind antigen autonomously. HCAbs are highly thermostable and reach enzyme active sites, cryptic pockets, and conserved viral surfaces inaccessible to conventional antibodies. records.title: Blockade of the angiogenin–5′-tiRNA-Glu− CTC axis attenuates age-related bone loss
affiliations: Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University
records.abstract: With aging, the accumulation of oxidative stress and cellular senescence drives the progression of osteoporosis. As a conserved cellular stress response, ribonucleases cleave cytoplasmic transfer RNAs (tRNAs) to generate tRNA-derived stress-induced RNAs (tiRNAs) with versatile functions. However, their biological functions in regulating osteoporosis remain poorly understood. In our study, we observed increased angiogenin (ANG) levels in aged Bone Marrow Stromal Cells (BMSCs) and found that ANG promotes age-dependent accumulation of 5’-tiRNA-Glu − CTC by cleaving tRNA-Glu under oxidative stress. The 5’-tiRNA-Glu − CTC disrupts the stability of anti-senescence and pro-osteogenic mRNAs, leading to bone-fat imbalance and thereby accelerating bone loss. Therapeutically, targeted suppression of 5′-tiRNA-Glu − CTC via an Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO)-based strategy effectively rescued ANG(S28N)-induced and age-associated bone loss. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of ANG with NCI-65,828 mitigated BMSC senescence and bone loss. Clinically, elevated serum levels of 5’-tiRNA-Glu − CTC negatively correlated with bone formation markers in osteoporosis patients, suggesting its potential as an associated biomarker for diagnosing age-related osteoporosis. records.title: Benchmarking relational graph convolutional networks for glioblastoma biomarker discovery via ceRNA and copy number variation analysis
records.abstract: Introduction Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a 5-year survival rate of 6.9%, attributable in substantial part to the shortage of reliable biomarkers. Competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) and copy number variation (CNV) analyses each carry biomarker identification potential, but existing work treats them separately. Methods We built a heterogeneous ceRNA graph over 2,075 differentially expressed loci, added gene-level copy number, and evaluated relational graph convolutional networks (RGCNs) against graph and non-graph baselines under 10-fold cross-validation. We then introduced a set of controls that separate the network signal from properties of the label set. Results The RGCN discriminated best among the graph architectures tested (AUCROC 0.874 ± 0.070 ), and a late-fusion ensemble with the CNV branch scored highest overall ( ( 0.883 ± 0.072 ) ). A logistic regression on one-hot node type alone, using no topology, reaches 0.824 ± 0.139 . records.title: Engineering, production, and biochemical characterization of a human CTLA-4 and IL-10 bispecific fusion protein
affiliations: Edmond and Lily Safra Children's Hospital
records.abstract: Introduction Bispecific fusion proteins represent a promising strategy for managing complex inflammatory diseases by potential simultaneous binding and modulation of multiple immune pathways. The cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) and interleukin-10 (IL-10) are potent immune suppressors that interact with CD80/86 and IL-10R, respectively. While Fc-fused CTLA-4 is clinically approved, the therapeutic development of IL-10 has been hampered by unpredictable immunostimulatory side effects. Fusing these domains offers a potential approach to leverage their combined immunomodulatory capacities. Herein, we biochemically characterized the binding of the engineered fusion protein to its cognate receptors. Methods A fusion protein linking the extracellular domain of CTLA-4 to a fused IL-10 domain was engineered. The protein was expressed in Escherichia coli as an N-terminal GST-tagged variant refolded from inclusion bodies, and as a soluble Fc-tagged variant in mammalian CHO cells. Target specificity and apparent binding affinities were evaluated using ELISA and biolayer interferometry (BLI). Results The bacterial and mammalian expression yielded approximately 10 mg/L and 39 mg/L of purified fusion protein, respectively. records.title: Prospective digital neurocognitive and patient-reported symptom monitoring in adults scheduled for CAR T-cell therapy: feasibility and exploratory patient-level observations from a single-center cohort
records.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate completion of individually tailored digital neurocognitive and symptom assessments in adults scheduled for CAR T-cell therapy and explore longitudinal changes in task-specific outcomes. METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort (n = 33), NeuroCAT comprised 25 cognitive, visual, and graphomotor tasks and a symptom questionnaire at baseline (T0). At early post-infusion (T1) and pre-discharge (T2), investigators selected approximately eight tasks per participant. RESULTS: All 33 patients completed T0, and 30 (90.9%; Wilson 95% confidence interval, 76.4-96.9%) completed both T1 and T2 assessments. Two patients died before follow-up, and one did not undergo follow-up after interruption of the planned treatment pathway due to clinical instability. Paired quantitative T0/T2 observations were available for only 4-11 patients per task, with heterogeneous changes in task-specific indices and patient-reported symptoms. Among three patients with chart-documented grade 1 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), one had increased fatigue and neuropathic pain ratings and another had increased dizziness and concentration-difficulty ratings. Nonspecific symptom worsening was also observed in patients without ICANS. CONCLUSION: Completion of individually assigned follow-up assessments was high among enrolled patients. records.title: Daratumumab, bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone for transplant-eligible elderly patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (KMM2101 trial)
affiliations: The Catholic University of Korea Seoul St. Mary's Hospital
records.abstract: Evidence supporting daratumumab, bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (D-VRd) in transplant-eligible patients aged 65–69 years with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) remains limited, particularly among Asian patients. Furthermore, the efficacy of six cycles of D-VRd induction before autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) has not been prospectively evaluated. In this multicenter, single-arm, phase II study, 26 transplant-eligible patients aged 65–69 years with NDMM received six cycles of D-VRd induction followed by ASCT. Maintenance therapy consisted of daratumumab plus lenalidomide for 12 months, followed by daratumumab monotherapy for another 12 months. The primary endpoint was the rate of very good partial response (VGPR) or better after ASCT. All patients completed induction, and 25 (96.2%) underwent ASCT. The VGPR or better rate after ASCT was 96.2%. The MRD-negative rate was 92.3%, and 65.4% achieved sustained MRD negativity for 12 months. After a median follow-up of 42.5 months, 3-year progression-free and overall survival rates were 76.9% and 88.5%, respectively. Grade ≥ 3 neutropenia was the most common adverse event, while dose intensity was generally maintained. Six cycles of D-VRd induction followed by ASCT and fixed-duration daratumumab-based maintenance achieved deep and durable responses with manageable toxicity in fit, transplant-eligible patients aged 65–69 years.

records.title: Ubiquitin-specific peptidase 10 as a context-dependent deubiquitination hub: integrating stress adaptation, disease progression, and therapeutic opportunities
records.abstract: Ubiquitination is a reversible post-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, and signaling, while deubiquitinases provide dynamic control over ubiquitin-dependent protein fate. Among these enzymes, ubiquitin-specific peptidase 10 (USP10) has emerged as a highly context-dependent regulator of cellular homeostasis and disease. USP10 influences diverse biological processes, including tumor progression, fibrotic remodeling, mechanotransduction, mitochondrial quality control, metabolic adaptation, and cellular stress responses. Its biological effects are often divergent: in some settings, USP10 supports protective pathways by stabilizing wild-type p53, promoting AMPK-dependent metabolic checkpoints, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and enhancing stress adaptation. In chronic disease contexts it drives pathology by stabilizing oncogenic or profibrotic substrates, including mutant p53, β-catenin, YAP/TAZ, EIF4G1, integrins, and SMAD4. In chronic inflammatory microenvironments, USP10 reinforces disease-promoting signaling through the NEMO/NF-κB and S100A9-SYK-NLRP3 inflammasome axes, increasing inflammatory mediators such as TNF-α, IL-6, CCL2, S100A9, caspase-1/GSDMD, ROS, and profibrotic TGF-β/CTGF pathways. This review synthesizes the dual and context-specific functions of USP10 across cancer, fibrosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tissue injury. records.title: GCLC-dependent glutathione restrains NK cell-driven inflammation in tumor and autoimmune disease
records.abstract: Glutathione (GSH) is a major intracellular redox buffer, but how GSH synthesis by glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit (GCLC) shapes natural killer (NK)-cell survival and effector function in tumor immunity and autoimmune inflammation remains unclear. Here, we investigated the consequences of Gclc deletion using NK-cell-specific and hematopoietic mouse models, tumor and autoimmune disease models, and human samples. Gclc deletion reduced NK-cell abundance, proliferation, survival, and terminal maturation across several tissues, but surviving NK cells showed enhanced acute effector responses. Mechanistically, GCLC dependent GSH regulates NK cell responses through the ROS-HIF-1α signaling pathway. NK cells in tumors and autoimmune diseases exhibit opposite levels of GCLC expression. High expression of GCLC in NK cells in tumors can inhibit their expression of HIF-1α and cytokines, thereby impairing their tumor control ability. NK cell GCLC expression decreases in RA and is associated with increased HIF-1α and effector factors. In summary, the synthesis of GSH dependent on GCLC shapes the effect of NK cells through the HIF-1 signaling pathway in a disease environment dependent manner, which is a key factor determining NK cell responses in tumor immune control and autoimmune inflammation.
